title: Deploy safety mesh for hosted API deployment pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The hosted API pipeline currently executes blue/green deploys and regional rollouts but lacks an integrated ‘safety mesh’ to enforce version-channel compatibility, multi-metric rollout gates, and a fast cross-region kill-switch. This leaves us exposed to slow regressions that only surface after broad traffic shifts and manual rollbacks that are error-prone.

Proposal: Deliver a safety mesh layer that sits above the existing deployment controller and provides:
- Version handshake and LTS channel enforcement (stable, beta, nightly) so routers only send traffic to compatible runtime/model pairs.
- Gate engine that evaluates multiple telemetry signals (p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, token-cost delta, model-quality regression score) before increasing traffic.
- Region-aware traffic shaping: automated, weight-based traffic shifts with adjustable step sizes and per-region kill-switch and quarantine routes.
- Automated rollback orchestration with pre-warmed target pools and coordinated KV cache invalidation to avoid cold-cache spikes.
- Integration with Console for runbook triggers, per-route dashboards, and realtime rollback buttons.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Schema & policy: define version labels and compatibility rules; introduce LTS tag semantics in model catalog and runtime manifest (work with model-onboarding).
2) Gate engine prototype: implement a small rule evaluator in the controller that can take threshold configs and evaluate against metrics from Observability API.
3) Traffic shaper: extend the traffic controller to accept step-based schedules, per-region weights, and an emergency kill-switch that reroutes to a fallback variant.
4) Rollback orchestration: build coordinated rollback workflow that drains connections, switches traffic, and runs cache quiesce + warmup tasks.
5) Console UX & runbook: add UI controls for manual overrides and a one-click rollback; surface gate reasons and expected impact.
6) Tests & staging: exercise in internal staging across three regions; inject failures (latency, error spikes, quality regressions) and verify gates and rollback behavior.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Strict vs permissive gates: we will start with conservative defaults (smaller step sizes) to prioritize availability; plan to loosen as confidence grows.
- Synchronous vs asynchronous evaluation: initial gate checks will be synchronous for first N minutes of rollout to enforce immediate safety, then shift to asynchronous checks for long-term ramping.
- Pre-warm complexity: pre-warming reduces cold-cache cost but increases resource usage; make pre-warm optional per release config to control spend.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field for granular checks and guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Gate engine evaluates latency, 5xx error rate, token-cost delta, and quality regression within 60s of metric emission.
Regional rollout can advance in adjustable steps (configurable default: 10% every 5m) and be paused by gate failure or manual intervention.
Emergency kill-switch reroutes traffic to a pre-configured fallback variant within 30s and surfaces reason in Console.
Automated rollback completes without more than 15% traffic blip relative to pre-deploy baseline and KV cache warmup reduces subsequent latency spike < 25%.
Console surfaces gate status, per-route telemetry, and one-click rollback that triggers orchestration workflow and runbook.
Unit/integration tests cover gate evaluation logic, traffic shaping arithmetic, and rollback orchestration; end-to-end staging run demonstrates behavior under injected failures.
Documentation and runbook published: update /runbooks/hosted-deploy-safety-mesh and console docs.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Rafael O: Spiked a prototype gate evaluator; it can parse threshold expressions and query metrics from the Observability API. Needs better RBAC for who can change gate configs.
2026-03-04 - Maya C (creator): Confirmed LTS semantics with model-onboarding team: 'stable' implies no rolling incompatibilities, 'beta' allows minor compatibility warnings. Added to project charter.

2026-03-06 - Priya N (SRE): Tested emergency kill-switch in dev cluster; observed 18s median time-to-reroute due to DNS propagation on our edge layer -- plan to add HTTP-level circuit breaker to cut traffic faster.
2026-03-08 - Rafael O: Integrated console button prototype with orchestration API. UX team requested clearer gate failure reasons and suggested showing last metric delta and sample traces inline.

2026-03-10 - Eng Lead (review): Approved initial rollout cadence but requested adjustable default step (from 10% to 5%) for high-risk routes and added requirement to run a canary against a QA prompt set for quality regression detection.
